analyst.summary: Bharat Forge had a genuinely mixed FY26: full-year profit grew a healthy double-digit rate, but the March-2026 quarter alone saw the parent company swing to an outright loss because of a Rs 450 crore write-down on its electric-vehicle bet (Tork Motors/Kalyani Powertrain) - management itself called this an admission that the EV strategy needs a fresh look. Layered on top were one-off costs from new labour-law rules and the wind-down of a loss-making German subsidiary. The real growth story going forward is defence and aerospace - a Rs 10,961 crore order book with several large, genuinely signed contracts (Navy turbine generators, a record carbine order, unmanned-systems deals) - plus a recovering US heavy-truck export cycle. But the stock has already priced in a lot of this: it has roughly doubled from its 52-week low and now trades near 90-100 times last year's profit, a multiple that assumes years of uninterrupted 25%+ growth across the whole company. Our own forward growth estimate is a more modest 13-15% once the mature core auto-forgings business, the shrinking European operations, and the risk that the current US truck-export surge is a pre-buy rush (ahead of 2027 US emissions rules) rather than a durable trend are accounted for. We rate this a Sell on valuation grounds - a real and improving defence/aerospace story, priced well beyond what that story alone can support.
